"The search for an Indian tourist who fell into a sinkhole in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia has been suspended due to safety concerns. Vijaya Lakshmi Gali was walking on a road on August 23rd when the pavement suddenly collapsed beneath her, causing her to plunge into an eight-meter-deep hole.

***

Despite extensive rescue efforts, authorities have found no trace of the victim except for her slippers. The search operation has utilized tracker dogs, remote cameras, and ground-penetrating radar technology over the course of eight days.

***

According to Malaysia's fire and rescue department, the operation was halted because it was deemed too risky to send divers down into the sinkhole. Dr Zaliha Mustafa, a minister in the prime minister's department, cited the safety and health of rescue personnel as primary factors in the decision.

***

* Rescuers attempted various methods including high-pressure water jets to flush the underground drainage system and excavators to remove debris, but two divers who entered on Thursday were pulled out before reaching the obstacle due to dangerous conditions.

***

Officials noted that a soil slip had been reported at the same location the previous year. Is there anything else I can help with?"
